The elevation of most neighborhoods in Miami averages around 6 ft (1.8 m) above sea level.
Miami's highest points are found along the Miami Rock Ridge.

The surface bedrock under the Miami area is called Miami oolite or Miami limestone.
Miami has a tropical monsoon climate with hot and wet summers and warm and dry winters.
Miami's sea-level elevation, coastal location, position just above the Tropic of Cancer, and proximity to the Gulf Stream shape its climate.
Average winter high temperatures range from 76.4–80.3 °F (24.7–26.8 °C).
January is the coolest month with an average daily temperature of 68.2 °F (20.1 °C).
Low temperatures fall below 50 °F (10 °C) about 3 to 4 nights during the winter season.
Miami has two basic seasons: a hot and wet season from May through October, and a warm and dry season from November through April.
Daily thundershowers occur in Miami during the hot and wet season due to humid unstable air masses.
The rainy season typically begins on the first day that the average daily dew point temperature is above 70 °F (21 °C).
